questions.question: Pass 1 (Information Architecture) — Finding 1: The action group has no visual hierarchy. Save, Reset, Cancel, and Export are all styled the same. Users must pause to identify the primary action — a hierarchy failure at the most critical part of the page. DESIGN.MD already specifies the fix. Apply it to the plan? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-save-button-primary>

options.label: Apply DESIGN.MD tokens (Recommended)
options.description: Save = filled #1d4ed8 with white text; Reset/Cancel/Export = neutral ghost buttons. Destructive intent communicated via confirmation dialog, not button color. Spec goes into the plan with exact tokens.

options.label: Add spec without tokens
options.description: Note that Save should be visually primary but leave exact colors to implementation. Less rigid; risks inconsistency with DESIGN.MD when implemented.

options.label: Defer — handle in implementation
options.description: Leave the gap as-is. The implementer decides at build time. Risk: ships with flat hierarchy because the gap is already the status quo.

questions.question: Pass 2 (Interaction States) — Finding 2: The plan references 'the existing form skeleton' for initial loading but gives no visual spec. Which fields are skeleton shapes, how wide, how tall? Without this every implementer ships a different skeleton. Add a brief spec to the plan? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-skeleton-spec>

options.label: Add skeleton spec to plan (Recommended)
options.description: Specify: two text-field skeleton rects (Display name, Email) + two switch-row skeleton rects (Weekly digest, Product tips), matching 640px max-width, using existing skeleton animation and color tokens. Enough detail that any implementer ships the same shape.

options.label: Leave as 'existing form skeleton'
options.description: Trust the existing component to handle it. Risk: existing skeleton may not match the current form structure, and no one catches it until visual QA.

questions.question: Pass 5 (Design System) — Finding 3: Spacing is inconsistent — 24px between some areas, 32px between others, 16px in a third. DESIGN.MD specifies an 8px base: sections 32px, field groups 24px, label-to-input 8px. Apply the consistent scale to the plan? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-spacing-scale>

options.label: Apply DESIGN.MD spacing scale (Recommended)
options.description: Section gaps = 32px, field group gaps = 24px, label-to-input = 8px. Removes the ad-hoc 16px section gap. Spec written into plan with exact values so implementer has no choices to make.

options.label: Defer to implementation
options.description: Let the implementer reconcile spacing at build time. Risk: inconsistent rhythm ships, and QA cycles are needed to catch it post-implementation.

questions.question: Pass 4+5 (AI Slop / Design System) — Finding 4: The form currently uses three font sizes: 14px, 16px, and 18px. This is two problems: (1) 14px violates the Universal Rule — body text below 16px is never allowed; (2) DESIGN.MD specifies exactly two roles: 16px for body/labels, 20px for section headings. Collapse to the DESIGN.MD two-size scale? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-typography-scale>

options.label: Apply DESIGN.MD two-size scale (Recommended)
options.description: Body/form labels/helper text = 16px. Section headings (Profile, Notifications) = 20px. Eliminates 14px (Universal Rule violation) and 18px (DESIGN.MD misalignment). Two sizes instead of three creates stronger, scannable hierarchy.

options.label: Keep 16px and 18px, just fix 14px
options.description: Raises 14px to 16px but keeps 18px headings instead of 20px. Fixes the hard rule but stays misaligned with DESIGN.MD typography spec. Three-size scale persists.

questions.question: Pass 5 (Design System) — Finding 5: Error text currently has ~3:1 contrast (red on light pink) — below WCAG AA minimum of 4.5:1. Users with low vision cannot reliably read error messages. DESIGN.MD specifies error.text #991b1b on error.surface #fef2f2 (approximately 5.5:1 contrast, passing AA). Apply the DESIGN.MD error color tokens? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-error-contrast>

options.label: Apply DESIGN.MD error tokens (Recommended)
options.description: error.text: #991b1b on error.surface: #fef2f2. Achieves ~5.5:1 contrast — passes WCAG AA (4.5:1). Also requires an icon and explicit text per DESIGN.MD (never color alone to communicate status). All three together go in the plan.

options.label: Defer to implementation
options.description: Leave the contrast gap noted but unresolved. Risk: a WCAG AA violation ships. Downstream: legal exposure and/or failing audit.

questions.question: Pass 5 (Design System) — Finding 6: Save takes 2–5 seconds with no feedback. The page appears frozen. This is the trust-critical moment: the user just committed their preferences. DESIGN.MD specifies an inline spinner beside 'Saving…' inside the disabled Save button, with aria-busy=true and reduced-motion support. Apply this pattern to the plan? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-save-spinner>

options.label: Apply DESIGN.MD pending-action pattern (Recommended)
options.description: Inline spinner inside disabled Save button. Button text changes to 'Saving…'. aria-busy=true on the button. @media (prefers-reduced-motion): spinner hidden, text-only 'Saving…' shown. Resolves the frozen-page trust erosion at step 6 of the user journey.

options.label: Add a page-level loading overlay instead
options.description: Blur or disable the entire form while saving. Covers the full wait period but is heavier UX — user loses context of what they just edited. DESIGN.MD specifies inline pattern; this diverges.

options.label: Defer to implementation
options.description: Leave the 2–5s frozen page as-is. Risk: users double-click Save, submit twice, or navigate away mid-save.

questions.question: Pass 6 (Responsive & Accessibility) — Finding 7: The plan specifies Weekly digest and Product tips as switches, but never names the keyboard interaction. ARIA switch role requires Space to toggle and aria-checked to announce state. Without this spec, an implementer may ship a custom element with no keyboard support — an accessibility regression. Add the switch keyboard pattern to the plan? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-switch-keyboard>

options.label: Add switch keyboard spec to plan (Recommended)
options.description: Weekly digest and Product tips use input[type=checkbox][role=switch] or equivalent. Space toggles the switch. aria-checked reflects current state. State change announces immediately via the existing aria-live region. This is the ARIA switch pattern; costs nothing to specify now.

options.label: Trust existing switch component
options.description: If an existing switch/toggle component already handles this, no spec change is needed. Risk: if the component is custom or third-party, keyboard support may not be guaranteed. Requires knowing the existing component's a11y coverage.

answers.Pass 6 (Responsive & Accessibility) \u20: Add switch keyboard spec to plan (Recommended)

questions.question: Design review complete — 6/10 → 9/10. All 7 decisions resolved. The plan is design-complete; next is the required shipping gate. What’s next?

options.label: Run /plan-eng-review (Recommended)
options.description: Eng review is the required shipping gate. It validates architecture, component wiring, tests, and accessibility implementation against the 7 approved design decisions. This design review added interaction specs (spinner, skeleton, switch keyboard), so eng review needs to validate their architectural fit.

options.label: Skip — I’ll handle next steps manually
options.description: End the review workflow here. The improved plan is at the e2e output path; implementation can begin. Run /plan-eng-review later before shipping.
